problemsFound: Image IMG_0987-2.JPG was described as CJ 'playing saxophone' on the jetty. He is actually seated at the end of the jetty with the saxophone resting beside him.

The homepage destination pairs were mis-split. The headings are Ibiza (Ushuaia), Amalfi Coast (Villa Cimbrone), D'Maris Bay (Nusr'et Restaurant) and Cape Town (MolenVliet Vineyard). The record listed D'Maris Bay and Nusr'Et Restaurant as two separate destinations.

rio-wedding.jpg was described as 'the Ferdinand wedding celebration'. The site only gives the filename 'rio-wedding' and shows the photo under the homepage heading 'D'Maris Bay – Nusr'et Restaurant'. The description has been reworded to match.
The 'Peak / off-peak' service put the 'discounted off-peak prices on enquiry' statement on the homepage. That line is on /packages/; only the season table is on the homepage.

The 'Event planning' service was sourced to /contact. That page has neither the 'Event Planner' site title nor 'Event Planning Advice'. It has been re-sourced to the homepage, and the advice item stays with the DJ package on /packages/.

The equipment list was inaccurate. Standard kit includes both an Equinox Black DJ Booth and an Equinox White DJ Booth, not 'an Equinox DJ booth'. The extras list left out 'QSC K12.2 12″ Tops x 2'. The Chauvet unit is listed on the site as 'INTIMSPOT 375ZX'.

The record said the SoundCloud 'profile URL not exposed', which is wrong. https://soundcloud.com/cjsaxlive is in the site's JSON-LD sameAs and on the Linktree, and it returns HTTP 200 with og:title 'CJ SAX LIVE'.

Verified channels were missing: the Linktree (linktr.ee/cj_sax, linked from the YouTube channel description), Mixcloud (mixcloud.com/cjsaxlive), and the 'Back to CJ's' podcast on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. The second Instagram (@cjsaxlive_events) is confirmed as 'Events Instagram' on the Linktree.
The TikTok gap is out of date. TikTok oEmbed now returns HTTP 200 with a player iframe for both videos embedded on the site (7547801132941249814 and 7106781707906354438).
The Gosfield Hall HD transcode was not checked before. It is now HEAD-verified: export_1674049374154_mov_hd.mp4 returns 200, video/mp4, 20,737,324 bytes.

The record included the video 'bookings: …' (somebody-else's-guy-1.mp4), whose poster shows only a female vocalist. That breaks the record's own rule of excluding network-artist footage, so it has been dropped.

Attribution of wedding-botleys-mansion-cj.m4v is weaker than claimed. Its sibling upload botleys-mansion-cj.m4v is titled 'DJ Jack @ Botley's Mansion', so 'cj' in a filename does not prove CJ performs in it. The poster shows only the couple on a staircase. It is now marked as performer-unclear.
The business's email address had been copied into video descriptions via the media titles. It has been removed to comply with the no-email rule for businesses other than The Bar People.
areasServed included 'UK-wide', which no fetched source states. It has been removed.

The namesake list was partly unverified. Two verified namesakes have been added. One is Christopher 'CJ' Johnson, a Los Angeles smooth-jazz saxophonist (ccjsax.com). The other is the Wayback Machine record showing cjsax.com in 2003–2005 belonged to an unrelated 'Charles Johnson, Jr.', so domain history before 2012 is not this business.
The 29:41 duration for YouTube JU8JF7zGRAk could not be confirmed, because the channel grid shows no duration badge for it. The duration has been removed.
The Booked Events listing shows 'Licenses & Insurance: No', while cjsax.com packages list Public Liability Insurance. The record did not note this conflict; it is now in gaps.

The record missed the historic site identity. A May 2013 Wayback capture of cjsax.com is titled 'CJ Turner', which matches the WordPress author slug 'cjturnersax'. It is added as an alternate name, with its source.

alternateNames: CJ Turner (cjsax.com site title in a May 2013 Wayback capture)
identity.evidence: I fetched the live Booked Events listing (https://bookedevents.co.uk/businesses/cj-sax/). It is titled 'CJ Sax – Booked Events' and shows Verified, Est. 2010, 'No Address', from £750 per event, 10–100 guests, and 'Listed on Dec 15, 2024'. Its 'Visit Website' button links href="https://cjsax.com", and its contact email is on the cjsax.com domain. The listing blurb ('CJ Sax Live is an International artist who made a name for himself playing on some of the world's biggest stages') matches word for word the opening line of the CJ SAX LIVE press pack image embedded at https://cjsax.com/2012/10/09/13/. The cjsax.com homepage title is 'CJ SAX LIVE - Event Planner, Saxophonist & DJ based in London', and its og:site_name says '…Wedding Sax & DJ in London. Event Planning & Entertainment in Essex.' So the trade, a saxophonist/DJ, matches the listing note. The listing thumbnail (CJ DJing with a saxophone on a boat) shows the same performer as the cjsax.com photos. The site header links Facebook (cj.sax.live), Instagram (cj_sax), TikTok (@cj_sax), YouTube (/cjsaxlive → @CJSAXLIVE) and Spotify. The YouTube channel's description ('I'm a saxophonist, DJ & event planner based in London!') links linktr.ee/cj_sax, which links back to www.cjsax.com. Namesakes checked and found to be different: Christopher 'CJ' Johnson, a Los Angeles smooth-jazz saxophonist (ccjsax.com); an unrelated 'Charles Johnson, Jr.' site that occupied cjsax.com in 2003–2005 (Wayback CDX), so domain history before 2012 is not this business; and J-SAX (Montreal), JSax (Elizabeth NJ) and TJ Sax (Holtsville NY). Year: the earliest WordPress media item and post on cjsax.com are dated 9 Oct 2012. The first Wayback capture of this business's site is May 2013 (titled 'CJ Turner'). The contact page says 'over a decade', and the press pack cites the London 2012 Olympics. This is consistent with 2010 but does not confirm it.

about.text: CJ SAX LIVE presents itself as an event planner, saxophonist and DJ based in London (site title). It offers wedding, corporate event and party hire (og:description).

The homepage describes CJ as a DJ and saxophonist who performs for high-profile clients. Past performances it names include the London 2012 Olympics and the Abu Dhabi F1, in places such as London, Dubai, Monaco, Ibiza, Marbella, Cannes, Mallorca and the Amalfi Coast.
The business supplies its own sound equipment and professional lighting. It also recommends and coordinates other live performers for weddings, corporate events and parties.

Its own words for its base are 'Based in London, creating vibes worldwide…'. The Destinations section lists Ibiza (Ushuaia), Amalfi Coast (Villa Cimbrone), D'Maris Bay (Nusr'et Restaurant) and Cape Town (MolenVliet Vineyard).

The CJ SAX LIVE press pack image on this page says CJ launched his own events company and works with high-profile and celebrity clients. UK venues it lists: The O2, the Tower of London, The Dorchester, Ronnie Scott's and The Ivy Asia. Ibiza: Ushuaia, Ocean Beach, Hard Rock Hotel, Space and Atzaro. Dubai: STK, Drais, White, Asia Asia, Five The Palm and Cirque le Soir. Rest of the world: the Maldives, Amalfi Coast, Sicily, Marbella, Cannes and the Himalayas. Sporting events: the Abu Dhabi and Monaco F1 Grand Prix and the London 2012 Olympics.

The contact page says the business has provided event services 'for over a decade'. 'Happy clients' it names: Billie & Greg Shepherd (The Mummy Diaries), Tommy & Georgia Fordham (Lobster Club, Mallorca), Mr & Mrs Ferdinand (London, UK) and Mr & Mrs Goldstein (Cap Rocat, Mallorca).

The packages page shows past events labelled Nusr'Et Restaurant / Salt Bae, The Maldives / Billie & Greg's Wedding, London / Rio Ferdinand OBE, and Ibiza / Tinie Tempah. It also says discounted off-peak prices are available, subject to availability and upon enquiry.
The Mixes page describes an open-format music policy that reads the crowd. Genres run from 70s/80s Soul to Club Classics, House, Dance Anthems, Old School RnB and Garage.
The homepage quotes a bride testimonial: 'We honestly can't thank you enough for making our day so special, you really went above & beyond!' — Jodie, Botley's Mansion.
The packages page quotes a client testimonial: '…you're the best dj they'd ever seen and you made the night.' — Ami, London.
The YouTube channel description reads: 'I'm a saxophonist, DJ & event planner based in London!' It points to CJ's 'Back to CJ's' podcast on Spotify and Apple Music.
The TikTok profile (nickname 'CJ SAX LIVE') has the bio 'DJ • Saxophonist • Party Starter' and links www.cjsax.com.

A May 2013 archived copy of cjsax.com was titled 'CJ Turner'. Its menu included Artist Management, Charity, 'Saxman to the Stars' and 'The Saxual Soirée'. It announced 2013 performance trips to Marbella and Ibiza and a Saxual Soirée night at NuBar, Loughton, UK.

On the Booked Events listing, CJ Sax is shown as verified, established 2010, catering for events of 10–100 guests, and priced from £750 per event. It was listed on 15 Dec 2024 and last updated 12 Jan 2025.

services.name: CJ SAX LIVE (live saxophone)
services.description: Live saxophone by CJ, improvising alongside your DJ. Includes a wireless sax microphone, public liability insurance, an event contract and invoice, and WhatsApp support. Published price, verbatim: 'Prices start from £1,000, subject to date & location'.

services.name: CJ SAX DJ LIVE (sax + DJ)
services.description: Live saxophone and DJ performance by CJ. Includes a sound system, DJ lighting and accessories, wireless sax and vocal microphones, event planning advice, public liability insurance, an event contract and invoice, and WhatsApp support. Published price, verbatim: 'Prices start from £3,000, subject to date & location'.

services.name: Recommended Artists
services.description: Musicians recommended from CJ's network: DJs, sax, bongos, violin, a magician and more. Clients negotiate directly with the performer. Published price, verbatim: 'Prices start from £375, subject to date & location'.

services.name: Seasonal / destination pricing periods
services.description: The homepage pricing table sets these periods: January–April is off-peak (Dubai/London), May–September is peak (worldwide), October is off-peak (Dubai/London), and November–December is peak (London). It promotes 'all inclusive entertainment packages'.

services.name: Sound, lighting & DJ booth equipment
services.description: Included as standard: Pioneer XDJ-AZ; QSC K12.2 12″ tops x 3; QSC KS118 18″ subs x 2; Equinox Black DJ Booth; Stellar 66 Multi FX LED x 2; Chauvet INTIMSPOT 375ZX; 200W LED moving head x 2; Equinox SpectraPix battens x 4; Equinox White DJ Booth. Extras: Pioneer XDJ-XZ; QSC K12.2 12″ tops x 2; Equinox Colour Raider uplighters x 8; Equinox Combi Booth; disco mirror balls x 4; foam glow sticks; Equinox 1.5m plinth x 2; QSC TouchMix 8.

services.name: DJ mixes / music policy
services.description: Open-format sets that read the crowd: 70s/80s soul, club classics, house, dance anthems, old-school RnB and garage. The page embeds four Spotify playlists ('70s & 80s Soul Classics', 'Sax Set - Main Set', 'Soul Disco', 'Commercial & Deep House') and two SoundCloud sets: 'CJ SAX Guest Set on Pure Ibiza Dubai 94.7 with Kieran Lindsay' and 'CJ's Studio: Ibiza Openings with The Garden Party UK'.

services.name: Event planning & performer coordination
services.description: The site title calls CJ an 'Event Planner, Saxophonist & DJ'. The homepage says the business recommends and coordinates other live performers for weddings, corporate events and parties.

A bride and guests dancing as CJ plays saxophone on a wedding dance floor.

CJ DJing outdoors at sunset with a mountain backdrop, in portrait orientation. It is shown on the homepage under 'Cape Town – MolenVliet Vineyard'.
CJ playing saxophone while standing in shallow water at an infinity-pool or sea edge, against a pale, hazy sky.
CJ's DJ setup in a venue: an LED star-cloth booth, QSC speakers, mirror balls on stands and moving heads. DJ-booth-1.JPG and DJ-booth-3.JPG (2048x1365) show the same setup.
CJ holding his saxophone with the Nusr-Et chef, labelled 'Nusr'Et Restaurant / Salt Bae' on the packages page. It features a celebrity.

record.tagline: Based in London, creating vibes worldwide…
gaps: The establishment year 2010 is not confirmed. The site says only 'over a decade'. Its earliest WordPress media item and post are dated 9 Oct 2012, and the press pack cites the London 2012 Olympics. Wayback shows that cjsax.com in 2003–2005 was an unrelated 'Charles Johnson, Jr.' site. This business's site is first captured in May 2013 (titled 'CJ Turner'), and cjsax.co.uk from July 2013.

The prices conflict. The directory says '£750 per event', but the current cjsax.com packages start at £375 (recommended artists), £1,000 (CJ SAX LIVE) and £3,000 (CJ SAX DJ LIVE), each 'subject to date & location'. The directory figure is not on the business's own site.
The Booked Events listing shows 'Licenses & Insurance: No', but every cjsax.com package lists Public Liability Insurance. This needs confirming with the business.
The current site does not give CJ's full name. The 2013 site title 'CJ Turner' and the WordPress author slug 'cjturnersax' suggest a stage name, but no current page states it.

No street address or postcode is published. The directory says 'No Address' and the site says 'based in London'. Hints of an Essex connection: og:site_name mentions Essex, a 2013 Saxual Soirée night was at NuBar, Loughton, and the 2019 brunch videos are at Chigwell Marquee. No current page states a location in Essex.

No genuine SVG logo exists. /logo.svg returns 404, the media library has no SVG, and the inline SVGs are only icons. The favicon is a cropped photo. The best mark is the 2196x868 transparent PNG wordmark. A separate 'Saxual Soirée' logo (2013–2015 uploads) belongs to an older event night, not the main brand.
The Booked Events gallery images for this listing (openart-image_*_raw.jpg in /2024/12/) are AI-generated OpenArt images, not real photos of the business, and should not be used.
The equipment page's product imagery is manufacturer shots and should not be used as business photos.
Several photos show celebrities (Rio Ferdinand, Salt Bae, Tinie Tempah) and named private clients. Publishing them may need the business's permission or image-rights consideration.
